_transcription: PAGE MAP: the booklet is 16 rendered pages (idx 0-15 = printed folios 1-16), every one accounted for. idx 0 = bilingual cover (Series AABB5/5, SET No. 2, Q.P. Code 57/5/2, BIOLOGY (Theory), 2 hours, 35 marks, 15 printed pages, 13 questions). ENGLISH = the EVEN indices 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 (folios 3-15). HINDI = the ODD indices 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13. The tops of all seven odd indices open in Hindi (idx 1 Hindi instructions and Q1-2, idx 3 Hindi Q3, idx 5 Hindi Q5-Q7, idx 7 Hindi Q8-Q12(a), idx 9 Hindi Q12(b), idx 11 Hindi Section C / Q13(a), idx 13 Hindi Q13(b)), so no English overflow onto an odd page and no parity inversion. idx 14 is English (Q13(b) in full); idx 15 (folio 16) is blank apart from a rule and the footer, checked at full size. The paper is born-digital; every row was read off the full-size page and its text layer was diffed against the vision read: they agree on every English line, and the text layer carries none of the figure labels, which were read off the page. Decimals: the paper prints ORDINARY full stops ('2.5 mg/kg'), left as printed; the scheme prints '1·15' with a raised dot, its own typography. Structure as printed: Section A Q1-6 @2, Section B Q7-12 @3, Section C Q13 case-based @5 = 35. Instruction (iv) says internal choices exist but gives no count; the roster was built from the scheme's bare ORs (text layer: four, all bare lines) and each confirmed against a printed OR on the paper: Q2, Q3, Q12 and Q13 (four alternatives). The '//' inside the scheme's Q8 answer is an alternative FORM of the answer (a PCR diagram), not an internal choice. Q11 prints (a) and (b) with no OR between them, so it is one row. FOLLOWER of 57/5/1: 15 of the 19 rows are 57/5/1 questions, each confirmed on this paper's own page (and against its text layer) and given 57/5/1's stem and context byte for byte (57/5/1 Q3a/b = Q2a/b, Q6a/b = Q3a/b, Q1 = Q4, Q4 = Q5, Q9 = Q8, Q7 = Q9, Q12 = Q11, Q10a/b = Q12a/b, Q13ai-iii and Q13b = Q13ai-iii and Q13b). New on this set: Q1 (Monascus purpureus and Trichoderma polysporum), Q6 (population density of a bacterial culture), Q7 (antibody types and diagram) and Q10 (Eli Lilly insulin), which replace 57/5/1's Q2 (biogas from human excreta), Q5 (banyan vs Parthenium density), Q8 (organ-transplant donor tests) and Q11 (ADA gene therapy). The five drawings (the four solar-radiation graphs, the S.T.P. flow diagrams, the vertebrate pie chart, the pBR322 map and the RNAi bar graph) were compared with 57/5/1's pages at full size and are the same drawings; the _figure notes were re-read on this paper's pages and the page indices are this PDF's. The scheme prints the same void note on Q3(b)(i) as 57/5/1 does on its Q6(b)(i). Quotes straight as printed; scientific names plain (Q1's Monascus purpureus and Trichoderma Polysporum print bold italic, Cynomolgus bold, Meloidogyne incognitia bold italic). Typos kept as printed: Q1 'Trichoderma Polysporum' (capital P), Q2(a) 'cocain', Q10 'Eli Lily', Q12(b)(ii) 'Extinction of species across taxa are not random.', Q13(a) passage 'Cloning of genes, play' and 'one such engineered vectors', Q13(b) passage 'An experiment was carried to study', Q13(b)(i) 'brings an effect', Q13(b)(iii) 'incognitia'. Three questions ask the student to draw (Q7 the antibody molecule, Q12(a)(i) the species-area graph, Q13(a)(iii) the EcoRI fragments), so three _drawFigure. No question examines content the rationalised NCERT book removed (Q6 is on population density, a live section), so no _outOfSyllabus.

questions.stem:
State the most important contribution of the following microbes for human welfare :
(a) Monascus purpureus
(b) Trichoderma Polysporum
State the mode of action of cocain on human body. Write the scientific name of the source plant it is obtained from.
Enumerate four most common warning signs of drug and alcohol abuse amongst the youth.

(i) Write the observations made at the end of Connell's field experiment on barnacles on the rocky sea coasts of Scotland.
(ii) Name any two categories of organisms that in general are adversely affected by competition.

questions.subtopic: Species Numbers and Patterns of Biodiversity
questions.stem:
The graphs (X) and (Y) given below depict the diurnal variations in the solar radiations in the month of June (Summer) and in December (Winters) :
(i) Which of the two graphs depicts tropical region and temperate regions respectively ?
(ii) Which of the two regions (X) or (Y) will show high biological diversity and why?
questions._figure: REQUIRED: four small graphs side by side, each of Solar radiation (y, arrow upward) against Time of the day (x, ticks 1 hr., 12, 24 hr.), each with one hump-shaped curve peaking at 12; the first two are captioned June 22 and Dec. 22 under the label (X), the last two June 22 and Dec. 22 under the label (Y). How tall each hump is, and so how much each region's radiation changes between June and December, is what part (i) asks the student to read, so it is withheld here. Page idx 4.
questions._cbseVoided: Note: Since graphs shown are not conclusive enough for drawing any interpretation, so one mark to be given to students, if attempted.
questions._flag: The void covers part (i) only (1 of the 2 marks); part (ii) is marked normally.

questions.stem: Ringworm is one of the most common infectious fungal disease in humans. Name any two genera of fungi which cause ringworm and state any of its two symptoms.

Study the given diagram of Sewage Treatment Plant (S.T.P.) and answer the questions that follow :
S.T.P. (Sewage Treatment Plant) (A): Municipal Sewage \(\rightarrow\) (W) BIOLOGICAL TREATMENT \(\rightarrow\) (X) SEDIMENTATION AND FILTRATION \(\rightarrow\) River
S.T.P. (Sewage Treatment Plant) (B): Municipal Sewage \(\rightarrow\) (Y) SEQUENTIAL FILTRATION \(\rightarrow\) (Z) BIOLOGICAL TREATMENT \(\rightarrow\) River
(a) Which one of the two 'S.T.P.' (A) or (B) will be more effective in treating the human excreta in the municipal waste?
(b) Write the steps followed in carrying the treatment of the sewage in step (Z), once the BOD of sewage is reduced significantly till it is passed on to the "anaerobic sludge digesters".
questions._figure: DECORATIVE: two flow diagrams, each a drawn building labelled Municipal Sewage feeding two boxes in sequence and then a drawn river; every box label, its letter (W, X, Y, Z) and the order of the boxes are carried as text in the stem, so the drawing adds nothing. Page idx 6.

questions.stem: What would be the best method to measure the total population density of a dense bacterial culture in a petridish and why ?

Different types of antibodies are produced in our body by the B-lymphocytes in response to a pathogen that enters in our blood. Name any two antibodies produced and draw a schematic representation of an antibody molecule and label its four parts.
questions._drawFigure: the antibody molecule as a Y: two long heavy chains forming the stem and the inner arms, two short light chains along the outer arms, joined by disulphide bonds; the four labels a marker wants are antigen binding site (at the tip of each arm), light chain, heavy chain and disulphide bond, with the N and C ends optionally marked.

questions.stem: A cell free method of amplifying DNA first developed in the mid 1980's revolutionized the field of biotechnology. Name the method and explain the basic steps of the technique involved.
'An HIV patient normally doesn't die of 'AIDS', but death is caused due to many other infections.' Do you agree with the statement ? Give explanatory reasons in support of your answer.
Explain how recombinant human insulin was prepared in 1983 by Eli Lily an American company.

(a) Enlist two criteria that are used to identify a region for maximum protection as 'Biodiversity hotspots'.
(b) Name any two "hotspot" regions in our country.

questions.subtopic: Species Numbers and Patterns of Biodiversity
questions.stem:
Given below is an equation describing the Species-Area relationship between species richness and area for a wide variety of taxa as angiosperm plants, birds, bats etc.
\(S = CA^{Z}\)
(i) Give a graphical representation of the given equation showing Species-Area relationship.
(ii) What does 'S' represent in the given equation ?
(iii) What is the value of 'Z' (regression coefficient) for frugivorous birds and mammals in the tropical forests of different continents ?
questions._drawFigure: the species-area graph: species richness (S) on the y-axis against area (A) on the x-axis, a curve rising steeply and then levelling off (a rectangular hyperbola) labelled S = CA^Z; the log-log form, a straight line labelled log S = log C + Z log A, may also be shown.

questions.stem:
Given below is a 'pie chart' representing the global biodiversity : proportionate number of species of major taxa.
(i) Identify (X) and (Y) in the given 'pie chart'.
(ii) "Extinction of species across taxa are not random." Which group amongst the vertebrates is more vulnerable to extinction.
(iii) Give one example each of recent extinctions of species in Russia, Mauritius and Australia.
questions._figure: REQUIRED: a pie chart headed Vertebrates with five shaded slices, one labelled Mammals, three labelled X, Y and Z, and one unlabelled. Which slice is largest and which is small, and so which taxon each letter stands for, is decided by the drawing, so the slice sizes and positions are withheld here. Page idx 10.

'pBR322' is one such engineered vectors developed by scientists. A diagram of an engineered vector pBR322 is given below :
questions.stem: Name the host for this cloning vector.
questions._figure: ILLUSTRATIVE: the case study's circular map of pBR322, attached so the passage's 'diagram ... given below' is not left dangling; this sub-part is answerable without it. Page idx 12.

5' --- GTACGAATTCCTGA---3'

questions.context:
RNA interference (RNAi) holds great potential as a therapeutic agent for the treatment of human diseases and as biocontrol agents in controlling pests in the field of agriculture. An experiment was carried to study the use of 'RNAi' for the potential treatment of disorders of cholesterol metabolism. Some people possess genetic mutations with elevated levels of ApoB gene which predisposes them to coronary artery diseases.

Lowering the amount of ApoB can reduce the number of lipoproteins and lower the blood cholesterol.

Tracy Zimmerman and her colleagues used RNAi in 2006 to reduce the level of ApoB in non human primates Cynomolgus monkeys.

One group of monkeys were given RNAi treatment (small interfering RNAs, SiRNAs) (doses 1 mg/kg SiRNAs), second group of monkeys were given RNAi treatment (doses 2.5 mg/kg SiRNAs) and third group of monkeys were injected with saline.

The results of the study are depicted in the graph below :
questions.stem:
(i) How does the treatment with 2.5 mg/kg brings an effect on cholesterol metabolism when compared from 24 hours and 144 hours.
(ii) Write any two natural sources from where dsRNA molecule could be obtained for silencing the specific mRNA.
(iii) How is RNAi used in controlling the infection on the roots of tobacco plants by the nematode Meloidogyne incognitia.
questions._figure: REQUIRED: a bar graph of Relative serum cholesterol (% predose) (y, 0 to 120 in steps of 20) against Time (hours) at 24, 48, 144 and 264 (x), with three bars at each time keyed Saline - X (diagonal hatching), 1 mg/kg - Y (dotted outline) and 2.5 mg/kg - Z (solid grey). The bar heights, and so how the 2.5 mg/kg bar changes between 24 and 144 hours, are what part (i) asks the student to read, so they are withheld here. Page idx 14.
